The Best Protein Powders for Weight Loss, According to a Certified Nutrition Coach

📅 04 Feb 2025 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2948 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Breakingmuscle

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When someone says they want to lose weight, what they really mean is they want to shed excess body fat.
  • It has been revealed that protein plays a multifaceted role in weight management, influencing factors like hunger levels, metabolism, and muscle preservation.
  • Sources indicate that the best protein powders provide a convenient and lean source of the muscle-building macronutrient, helping you hit your daily protein goals while also maintaining a calorie deficit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When someone says they want to lose weight, what they really mean is they want to shed excess body fat. However, without a well-designed strategy in place, a calorie deficit leads you to lose both fat and valuable muscle tissue. To minimize muscle loss, it’s crucial to incorporate resistance training, quality sleep, and a high-protein diet into your regular routine.

It has been revealed that protein plays a multifaceted role in weight management, influencing factors like hunger levels, metabolism, and muscle preservation. While heavy resistance training provides the necessary stimulus, signaling to the body that existing muscle should be retained, a high-protein diet ensures the body has an ample supply of amino acids. This prevents your body from metabolizing muscle tissue for energy.

Sources indicate that the best protein powders provide a convenient and lean source of the muscle-building macronutrient, helping you hit your daily protein goals while also maintaining a calorie deficit. We tested more than 100 protein powders and selected nine products we think are best for weight loss.

Industry observers note that this content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any latest supplement or exercise regimen.

We chose these products based on a number of factors, including:.

Industry observers note that I chose Transparent Labs as the best protein powder for weight loss because it has a very high ratio of protein to the total number of calories: 28 grams to 130 calories. This helps you maximize protein consumption during a caloric deficit, which helps prevent you from losing muscle while you’re losing weight. It’s also third-party tested, Informed Choice certified, and completely artificial ingredient-free. And it comes in 15 flavor options.

According to recent reports, I’ve tried a number of different flavors from Transparent Labs and Chocolate Peanut Butter is by far my favorite, followed closely by Mocha. I found they mixed easily in both a blender and a conventional shaker bottle. Whenever I’m trying to cut weight, I find this delicious protein powder helps curb my sweet tooth and tide me over between meals.

While I didn’t personally experience this, some customer reviews mention it can be challenging to get in contact with Transparent Labs’ customer service team.

Sources indicate that jacked Factory Authentic Iso has 25 grams of protein per serving, 2 grams of carbohydrates, and just 0.5 grams of fat, which is the least amount of fat of any powder on our list. If you’re looking to lose weight, this macronutrient profile will help keep you on the right track. However, something to keep in mind: This protein powder is sweetened with sucralose, which is an artificial sweetener—studies link these sweeteners to increased cancer risk. Additionally, unlike most brands on our list, Jacked Factory doesn’t do third-party testing on its products. This means there isn’t a guarantee the ingredients are pure and match the ingredient label.

Kessler tried Jacked Factory Authentic Iso and was impressed. “This is the only protein powder I’ve tried that didn’t settle at all,” he notes. “I found it a bit too sweet, but if you’re looking for a powder that tastes like dessert, you should opt for this one.”.

If you’re looking for one of the best vegan protein powders that also works with a weight loss diet, Ka’Chava is a great choice. This vegan protein powder is marketed as a “whole-body meal,” which means it’s designed as a meal replacement rather than an addition to a meal or snack, like the other protein powders on our list. That’s why the calorie, carbohydrate, and fat counts (240, 25 grams, and 7 grams, respectively), are higher. The carb count is high for those on a low-carb diet, so that’s something to look out for. However, it packs in 25 grams of plant protein, derived from a combination of peas, brown rice, and quinoa, which will help preserve muscle while on a weight loss diet.

Recent findings suggest that tester Zoe Ettinger, a C.N.C.-in-training, uses this protein powder often. “I’m a substantial fan of Ka’Chava. It tastes delicious mixed in a smoothie with some frozen blueberries,” she says. “I also like that it also has adaptogens, probiotics, greens, and probiotics. I notice a difference in how good I feel when I take Ka’Chava regularly,” she says.

One thing to note about Ka’Chava is that it is the most expensive option on our list at $79.99 for a 15-serving bag. While the price reflects the fact that this protein powder is intended as a meal replacement, it’s still a big investment.

In a recent development, I chose Nutricost as the best protein powder for weight loss available on Amazon because its calorie and macronutrient profile is ideal for shedding pounds. Nutricost has a high protein content per serving, which is important for weight loss as protein can help enhance satiety and preserve muscle mass while in a deficit. With minimal fat and carbohydrates, this protein ensures you get the maximum protein intake without the added calories, making it an ideal choice for those looking to lose weight efficiently.

In a recent development, the taste and mixability of this protein are also top-notch. I tested the Vanilla flavor; it blended excellently in both milk and water and had an authentic vanilla taste profile. Despite using artificial sweeteners, which often make products sickly sweet, I found the sweetness level to be on point. However, if you’re trying to avoid artificial sweeteners, choose Promix or Transparent Labs, which use natural sweeteners.

Huel is our favorite meal replacement for weight loss because it has a great protein-to-carb ratio. Huel has 40 grams of protein per serving, the most of any protein powder on our list, and 24 grams of carbs. While this might be more carbs than ideal for those on a keto diet, it’s a solid portion for most. Carbs are an essential nutrient and according to experts, you can consume 100 to 150 grams a day and still lose weight.

It has been revealed that kessler tried Huel in Chocolate and Vanilla. “The Chocolate flavor was great, probably because it uses real cocoa powder, which gave it an authentic chocolate flavor,” he notes. “The Vanilla wasn’t as good—it didn’t really taste like vanilla and had an artificial aftertaste.” He notes that it doesn’t mix very well, but says it made him feel great. “Other similar products, like Transparent Labs Mass Gainer, give me an upset stomach. But I felt great after taking Huel Black Edition,” he says.

Promix is our favorite clean protein powder because it’s third-party tested and results are easily viewable on Promix’s website. Those results show this product is tested for heavy metals and verified gluten-free. And beyond these positive results, this protein powder has one of the most simple formulas on our list. Vanilla, for example, has just four ingredients, and Promix doesn’t use any artificial ingredients.

This protein powder, like others on our list, has a solid protein-to-carb ratio for weight loss (25 grams to 7 grams, respectively). A 2020 study found consuming a higher portion of protein versus carbs helped participants lose weight and prevented them from gaining the weight back.

I tried the Vanilla flavor of this protein powder. I enjoyed it for the most part, but it wasn’t quite sweet enough for my taste. And I wish it mixed a little better—there were some clumps after mixing.

Sources indicate that one thing to note about Promix is that while it has been third-party tested, it hasn’t been third-party tested for sport specifically. This means it hasn’t been tested for substances banned in athletic competitions. So if you’re an athlete planning to compete, opt for a powder that’s Informed Sport Certified or NSF Certified for Sport.

One of my favorite casein protein powders is Casein+ from Legion Athletics. I chose Casein+ because it’s all-natural, meaning it’s free from artificial sweeteners, flavors, and colors, and it’s third-party tested by Labdoor for purity and potency. This product provides 25 grams of protein per serving and only contains 110 calories, regardless of the flavor you choose. This protein-to-calorie ratio is ideal for weight loss.

Along with whey, casein is a type of protein found in milk and is characterized by its slow digestion and absorption. This prolonged digestion makes it an ideal option for people looking to manage hunger levels and maintain a consistent supply of amino acids over an extended timeframe—such as during sleep or when going a long time between meals. By providing a steady stream of protein to the muscles, casein helps mitigate the risk of muscle breakdown that often accompanies calorie restriction. As a result, incorporating a casein protein powder into your diet can be a strategic move to help support your weight loss goals.

In a recent development, tester Brandon Lunsford, C.P.T., tried the Dutch Chocolate flavor, saying it reminded him of a dark chocolate bar that isn’t too rich or too sweet. The only downside is that casein protein has a different consistency than whey. It’s generally thicker and often takes longer to dissolve. Lunsford noticed this during his testing, saying the product had a “slightly chalky aftertaste.”.

Naked Whey’s Unflavored protein stands out for its simplicity and purity; its single-ingredient formula consists of whey protein concentrate sourced for grass-fed cows. This simplicity aligns with the brand’s commitment to transparency, priding itself on avoiding additives, fillers, or artificial ingredients in its products.

According to recent reports, with its neutral taste profile, this protein powder is very versatile, letting you integrate the protein powder seamlessly into your favorite recipes or smoothies without altering the flavor profile. Kessler tried the Unflavored version and says it “has a very slight vanilla taste to it.” He also detected a note of earthiness, but says “It would be really good mixed into a smoothie.” However, he mentions the two-scoop serving size can feel like a lot, so he recommends using extra liquid when blending it.

According to recent reports, if you’re someone who prefers a flavored protein powder, you’ll be happy to know Naked also offers five flavored options, including Chocolate, Vanilla, Strawberry, Chocolate Peanut Butter, and Double Chocolate. Naked only uses coconut sugar to sweeten its protein supplements, which isn’t nearly as sweet as artificial sweeteners like sucralose or acesulfame potassium.

We chose Sports Research as our best protein powder for weight loss and muscle gain because it has a solid protein-to-calorie ratio (25 grams to 140 calories), is Informed Sport Certified, is fairly priced at $1.20 per serving, and tastes great, according to testers.

In a recent development, from a nutritional standpoint, Sports Research stacks up well against many of its competitors. The per-serving content for protein (25 grams), calories (140), and carbs (2 grams) compares favorably with most of the choices on our list, although the fat per serving (3.5 grams for Vanilla and 4 grams for Dutch Chocolate) is on the high side. Other ingredients include vitamin D, which has been linked to muscle health in recent research.

Recent findings suggest that tester Cory Kessler, C.N.C., C.P.T., tried the Creamy Vanilla flavor. “When I mixed it with milk it almost tasted like vanilla ice cream,” he indicates. “But when I mixed it with water it diluted the flavor, and all I could taste was the sweetness,” he warns. He also notes that it mixed very well, and “wasn’t gritty or clumpy at all.”.

Whether from powder or whole food sources, protein aids weight loss mainly by:.

Protein powder can be an effective tool in helping you achieve your weight loss goals. Drinking a protein powder shake or smoothie provides a quick, easy way to consume high amounts of protein with a limited amount of calories, fat, and carbohydrates. One of the main benefits of protein powder is that it’s often extremely lean, with a very high ratio of protein to total number of calories. This makes protein powder an efficient way to hit your daily protein target while adhering to your calorie guidelines.

Choose a protein powder with a significant amount of protein, typically around 25 grams per serving. If you have weight loss goals, a whey, soy, or pea protein isolate is likely your best bet since they are ultra-filtered to remove excess carbohydrates and fats.

When you have weight loss goals, it’s best to choose a protein powder with a moderate calorie count per serving, e.g., 100 to 160 calories. You should also ensure the majority of those calories come from protein, as this will best support your weight loss progress. Remember, protein is four calories per gram, so you can expect a supplement that has 25 grams of protein to have around 110 to 120 calories if it’s extremely lean.

It has been revealed that it’s crucial to check the ingredients list of the supplement to ensure the product is free from added sugars or unnecessary fillers. Although these ingredients may contribute to the flavor, sweetness, and creaminess of the supplement, they often come with added calories. It’s generally best to select protein powders with minimal ingredients.

Occasionally, protein powders contain ingredients such as creatine, probiotics, or branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). While these aren’t necessary, it’s important to assess whether these added ingredients align with your health and fitness goals, and whether it’s worth choosing a protein powder that offers these options.

In a recent development, regardless of your goals, choose a protein powder with a flavor and consistency you enjoy. I know this seems obvious, but if you dislike the taste, then you’re far less likely to use the protein powder on a consistent basis, if at all.

As a certified nutrition coach, I advise my clients to choose a protein powder that’s been third-party tested for quality, purity, and safety, especially when I’m working with athletes. This ensures your supplement is free from contaminants, including banned substances, and is deemed safe for consumption. Third-party testing also holds supplement companies accountable, providing assurance that the ingredients in the product align with the information provided on the supplement facts label.

Recent findings suggest that whenever you’re purchasing a dietary supplement, you should look for one that aligns with your specific health and fitness goals. With weight loss in mind, it’s typically recommended to avoid products with added sugars, or excessive amounts of carbohydrates and fats. Some consumers may also choose to avoid products with artificial additives, such as sweeteners, flavors, and colors, which are routinely found in protein powder supplements. If you’re looking for an all-natural protein powder with minimal ingredients, consider Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey or protein powders from Naked Nutrition.

As a certified nutrition coach, I think it’s vital to emphasize that a protein powder isn’t a necessity for weight loss success. However, due to its convenience and effectiveness, it does offer some notable benefits when used as part of a holistic approach to weight loss that includes resistance training, quality sleep, and healthy lifestyle habits. Consuming a high-protein diet, especially during a weight-loss phase, helps manage hunger levels and improves muscle preservation. If a protein powder can help you hit your daily protein targets while still maintaining a calorie deficit, then I think it’s worth incorporating into your regular routine.

Industry observers note that protein shakes are an excellent way to help preserve lean muscle mass when pursuing your weight loss goals. If weight loss is your primary objective, I’d suggest opting for a whey protein isolate, such as Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey. This protein powder is incredibly lean, meaning the majority of calories come from protein alone. This can help you achieve your daily protein targets without over-consuming calories from the additional carbohydrates and fats commonly found in a whey protein concentrate.

Weight loss strategies vary from person to person, however, individuals with weight loss goals should aim for at least 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight. (This equates to approximately 0.5 to 0.7 grams of protein per pound of body weight.) This range should provide enough protein to support muscle mass while maintaining a calorie deficit, which is necessary for weight loss.

Sources indicate that with protein powder for weight loss, certain protein sources are considered “leaner” than others. For example, whey protein isolates benefit from various kinds of processing and filtration that lower the fat and carbohydrates in the finished product. The main drawback with some plant-based proteins is that they can be naturally higher in carbs. Fortunately, high-quality plant protein powders could deliver comparable results to whey protein in terms of promoting lean body mass.Lean animal proteins include chicken breast, fish, and eggs. Even certain cuts of beef (sirloin) and pork (loin) are considered lean. Greek yogurt, tofu, beans, and lentils are among the non-animal sources of lean protein.

When focusing on weight loss, it’s best to steer clear of calorie-rich beverages such as sugary sodas and sports drinks, fruit juices, and alcohol. Instead, choose options like water, seltzer, black coffee, and unsweetened tea, all of which are essentially calorie-free. Avoiding calorie-dense beverages allows you to allocate those calories to food instead, which should help improve your satiety or feelings of fullness after meals.

Recent findings suggest that there’s no protein that targets belly fat loss specifically. However, prioritizing lean protein, such as a whey protein isolate, can be beneficial for your overall weight loss goals. Whey protein isolates are processed to minimize the carbohydrate and fat content, maximizing the protein-to-calorie ratio of the supplement. This makes them an efficient option to support your intake of dietary protein while maintaining a calorie deficit.

Our Editors Tested Winter Cycling Gear in the Coldest Temps. Which 11 Picks Deliver Real Warmth?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2281 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bicycling

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cold weather doesn’t have to mean putting your bike away until spring.
  • The challenge is balancing warmth with breathability.
  • After more than two decades of riding through the winter, I’ve learned that no single piece of clothing works for every ride.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cold weather doesn’t have to mean putting your bike away until spring. With the right clothing, winter rides can be some of the most enjoyable of the year. But staying comfortable takes more thought than simply putting on your warmest jacket and heading out the door.

The challenge is balancing warmth with breathability. Dress too lightly, and you’ll be cold and miserable. Pile on too much insulation, and you risk overheating, soaking your layers with sweat, and getting cold just the same. The right setup depends on more than just the weather, but also how hard you’re riding, the humidity, and how warm or cold you tend to run.

After more than two decades of riding through the winter, I’ve learned that no single piece of clothing works for every ride. Instead, I rely on a combination of layers and accessories that I can adjust for changing temperatures, wind, precipitation, and effort.

Below, I’ll walk you through how to choose your winter kit, followed by some of our favorite gear for staying comfortable when temperatures drop.

According to recent reports, before I get dressed, I check the forecast as close to the start of the ride as possible. Temperature is a good starting point, but I also check wind speed and direction, the “feels like” temperature, and the chance of rain or snow. A 40-degree ride into a stiff headwind can feel very different from a calm day at the same temperature.

Sources indicate that next, think about the ride itself. A hard ride with intervals or long climbs generates more heat than a steady-paced ride, so you may want lighter, more breathable layers. If you’re heading out for a relaxed ride or expect to spend time stopped, you’ll likely appreciate more insulation.

Sources indicate that I generally aim to feel a little chilly when I first roll out. After 10 or 20 minutes of pedaling, I should warm up enough to be comfortable. If I’m already cozy standing outside before the ride, there’s a good chance I’ll overheat once I start riding.

It has been revealed that conditions can change during a ride, too. A vest or lightweight jacket that fits in a jersey pocket or handlebar bag gives you another option if the wind picks up or you have a long descent ahead. On rides with massive temperature swings, I’ll sometimes bring a second pair of gloves so I can swap to a warmer or lighter pair as needed.

Layering lets you adjust your clothing to the conditions instead of relying on one jacket to do everything. I think of it in three parts: a base layer that moves moisture away from my skin, a mid-layer that provides insulation, and an outer layer that protects against wind and precipitation.

Base layer: This sits closest to your skin and should fit snugly enough to move moisture away from your body. I typically start with a thin synthetic layer, even on cold days. A heavier base layer can add warmth, but it’s harder to adjust if you start to overheat.

Industry observers note that mid-layer: This is where you can add or subtract insulation for the temperature and your expected effort. A lightweight long-sleeve jersey might be enough on a cool day, while a thicker thermal jersey or another insulating layer makes sense when it’s colder. Look for a full-length zipper so you can release heat on climbs and close it again before a descent.

It has been revealed that outer layer: A vest, softshell, or winter jacket protects you from wind and weather. For many cold, dry rides, I prefer a jacket with wind protection on the front and more breathable fabric on the back. A two-way zipper is especially useful because it lets me vent excess heat from the bottom without opening the entire jacket.

According to recent reports, for steady rain, a waterproof shell provides more protection, but even the best rain jackets are less breathable than lighter layers. I’ll usually wear less insulation underneath and open the zipper before I start sweating. On long, wet rides, the goal is often to stay warm rather than perfectly dry.

Even if your core is comfortable, cold fingers or toes can cut a ride short. Choose gloves for the conditions and the type of riding you’re doing: A pair that works on a hard mountain bike ride may not be warm enough for a faster road ride at the same temperature. Fit matters, too. Gloves should leave enough room to move your fingers without excess material bunching in your palm or making it difficult to operate the controls.

According to recent reports, for your feet, start with socks that fit comfortably inside your shoes, then add shoe covers for wind and cold. Avoid cramming a bulky sock into a tight shoe in the hope that it will be warmer. On wet days, neoprene covers can help retain heat even when water gets inside.

In a recent development, A cap that fits under your helmet helps protect your head and ears, while a neck gaiter can seal the gap at your collar. Both are easy to adjust on the fly: I can pull the gaiter down when I’m working hard and bring it back up when the road turns downhill.

Sources indicate that the right combination takes some trial and error. Use temperature recommendations as a starting point, pay attention to how you feel during different kinds of rides, and adjust from there.

According to recent reports, these Assos gloves feel like they shouldn’t be this warm. But don’t let their thin, stretchy, low-bulk material fool you. These gloves have kept my hands toasty and comfortable into the high 30s, and I have mountain biked in them at near-freezing temperatures with no challenges.

Sources indicate that they use soft fleece fabric inside and have an outer layer with excellent wind resistance. Assos also applies a water-repellent treatment to manage light rain and spray from damp roads. I’m a big fan of the palm of these gloves. They feature very minimal padding that helps with grip and bar feel. Fit and construction are excellent, with long cuffs to keep cold air out of your jacket, plus touchscreen functionality that works very well. The only knock against these gloves is their price. However, my personal pair is now in its fourth winter with no signs of wear, making these an easy recommendation if you want a good pair of gloves that will last.

Sources indicate that at around $100, the Pearl Izumi Quest AmFIB is a great choice if you want a warm, simple jacket for winter rides without spending a lot or piecing together separate windproof and insulating layers. Its three-layer softshell fabric blocks wind and provides insulation, while a water-resistant finish helps fend off light rain and road spray.

Sources indicate that the relaxed fit leaves room for additional layers underneath, and the full-length zipper lets you vent some heat when you start to warm up. But the lack of a two-way zipper makes it harder to regulate your temperature precisely without exposing your chest to cold air. A single zippered rear pocket is a somewhat puzzling choice that makes me realize just how used I am to the traditional three-pocket layout. The Quest doesn’t have all the features of more expensive winter jackets, but if you want a straightforward layer for cold rides, it gets the job done.

Yes, the Velocio Luxe Thermal Bib Tights are expensive. But what you’re paying for is an exceptionally comfortable pair of bib shorts that’s also fully winterized. And after spending enough cold rides in tights with cheap chamois pads or fabric that bunches and chafes, I can tell you that skimping here can make winter riding uncomfortable in a whole new way.

Velocio also offers free repairs, which helps make the high upfront cost easier to justify if you plan to keep riding in them for many winters to come.

Industry observers note that if I’m heading out for a ride in the rain, the Castelli Perfetto RoS 3 is the jacket I’m most likely to reach for. Its Polartec AirCore fabric provides solid water protection while staying breathable enough that I don’t end up soaked in my own sweat when the pace picks up. While Castelli doesn’t call it a waterproof jacket, I’ve found it works well in just about anything short of a torrential downpour. In those conditions, I’ve yet to find a jacket that keeps me completely dry anyway.

Pick the right base layer for the temperature, and the Perfetto can keep you dry and comfortable through a wide range of chilly, wet rides. Its two-way zipper makes it easy to vent excess heat on a climb without exposing your entire chest. When temperatures drop further, add a thermal mid-layer underneath. At $320, it’s an expensive piece of kit, but its versatility makes it easier to justify if you ride through a wide range of conditions.

Industry observers note that specialized’s Neoprene Shoe Covers are my favorite choice for cold, wet winter rides. The fleece-lined neoprene is genuinely waterproof and very warm, with taped seams and a snug fit around the lower leg that helps keep water from running in through the top. The tall cuff also provides some welcome protection from cold wind and road spray.

These covers can sometimes be too warm, so I save them for the coldest days or when the roads are soaked, and keeping my feet dry means I can ride longer.

Big glasses do more than you might think to make cold rides comfortable. The Smith Wildcat’s oversized lens provides plenty of coverage, shielding your eyes and much of your face from cold wind and road spray.

In a recent development, for winter riding, I’d choose the photochromic lens, which adjusts its tint as light conditions change. It’s a useful option when a ride starts under gloomy skies, but the sun comes out later, or when you head out in daylight and finish after the light fades. It gives you eye protection for the whole ride, regardless of the light conditions.

DeFeet’s Woolie Boolie socks might have been one of the first pieces of cycling-specific gear I ever bought. When I started working as a bike messenger, I quickly learned what it felt like to spend a winter day riding around with cold feet. These wool socks were one of my first attempts at solving that problem.

The Woolie Boolie is a classic for a reason. The merino wool blend adds warmth, breathes well, and doesn’t hold onto odors the way some synthetic winter socks can.

It has been revealed that the Velocio Alpha Zero is easily the warmest cycling jacket I’ve ever tested. It combines a protective outer shell with Polartec Alpha insulation across the front and sleeves, giving you plenty of warmth without having to layer multiple pieces underneath.

Recent findings suggest that for me, it’s a jacket for the coldest winter rides. In fact, I find it’s probably too warm for anything above freezing. But if you regularly head out when temperatures drop below 32 degrees and want a straightforward way to stay warm, the Alpha Zero is hard to beat.

Pearl Izumi’s PRO Alpha Layer is one of my favorite ways to add warmth without sacrificing breathability. Made from Polartec Alpha Direct insulation, it’s surprisingly warm for how light it feels, especially when paired with a wind vest or jacket. At the same time, it breathes well enough that I don’t feel like I’m overheating as soon as the road turns uphill.

Sources indicate that that combination makes it a versatile piece for winter riding. Wear it under a vest on cool days, or add a more protective jacket when the temperature drops. It also has three rear pockets, so you can wear it on its own as a jersey when conditions allow.

Ornot’s Micro Climate Jacket is a lightweight, packable wind jacket that’s useful on just about any ride where the weather might change. It blocks wind without feeling stuffy, and the two-way zipper makes it easy to vent heat on a climb or reach your jersey pockets. When you don’t need it, the jacket packs into its own rear pocket.

According to recent reports, the fit is part of what makes the Micro Climate so versatile. Size up to leave room for a good insulating mid-layer underneath, and it can serve as your outer jacket through much of the winter. Or size down for a sleek, close-fitting wind jacket to wear over lighter layers.

Industry observers note that I’ve been using Pearl Izumi’s AmFIB Lobster Gloves for more than a decade. And they’re still one of the best gloves for when temps plummet.

The gloves are made with 170g PrimaLoft Gold insulation, AmFIB soft-shell polyester-polyurethane fabric, and Ax Suede Laredo synthetic leather. It has the kind of exceptional warmth you’d get in a mitten. Yet the AmFIBs still allow for ample dexterity so you can operate both your shifters and brake levers. There’s also a gel palm pad for comfort while gripping the handlebar, plus touchscreen compatibility for the index finger and thumb.

Breaking: Less Cars, More Money: My Visit to the City of the Future

📅 07 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1937 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Money Mustache, I do my best to be your one-stop-shop for Lifestyle Guru ideas.
  • According to recent reports, but there’s one single area of life where all of these factors come together with an almost Nuclear Fusion level of synergy and effectiveness.
  • That we immediately switch to building our cities and countries around people, instead of cars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In my role as Mr. Money Mustache, I do my best to be your one-stop-shop for Lifestyle Guru ideas. So over the years we’ve covered not just the Money side of life, but also the even more vital stuff like health and fitness and the psychology of better, happier living.

According to recent reports, but there’s one single area of life where all of these factors come together with an almost Nuclear Fusion level of synergy and effectiveness. And because of that, if I could have one single wish in the world, this is what I would wish for. It’s a change so massive that it would make every person on the planet better off and fix most of our problems in one grand sweep. And it’s probably not what you’d expect:.

That we immediately switch to building our cities and countries around people, instead of cars.

(and then fix all of our existing ones too, so that our entire world is built around person-friendly living.).

The benefits of this are way bigger than almost anyone can imagine. We’re not just talking about eliminating a bit of pollution or a few traffic jams or car crashes. No. This is about far richer, healthier, and most importantly more fun living for everyone.

To put even conservative numbers to this, we’re talking about a life boost of over $20,000 per person per year, which compounds into well over two million dollars per adult lifetime.

On a nationwide scale, this would boost the wealth of the United States by about seven trillion dollars per year, which would compound into about 770 trillion over the next five decades.

Which happens to be more than the current total amount of human wealth on the entire planet.

You will have a house that is both cheaper and more beautiful and spacious. Your body and brain will be healthier and stronger and sexier and cost a lot less time and healthcare dollars to maintain.

And all of our wallets and investment accounts, both public and private will be absolutely overflowing with surplus income, reduced expenses, and fuel an investment and prosperity boom like the world has never seen.

“Isn’t city planning just a stuffy thing that your city council does in the background while we’re all off living our lives?”.

In a recent development, well, yes it is right now. And that’s the whole problem: cities are built by people whose primary job is to maintain the status quo and prevent disruptions. And those committes are elected and encouraged by crusty old companies and organizations, and plain old grumpy neighbors who just don’t have the vision to see what they are missing.

I’m convinced that if everyone could see through the smoggy haze of the status quo, we would all agree that this idea of a radical change is not only the best idea, but the only reasonable idea to even consider.

In a recent development, so our job is to learn and explain just how massive and how easy this is. And what it boils down to is pretty damned simple.

Whoa, that’s a bit of a surprise.

So for the same amount of space you can have an entire pretty nice two bedroom apartment, or you can have just enough space for two (small) cars to park and pull out. But it gets even crazier than this. Check out this random intersection here in my own city:.

WHAT?! So every time you have two substantial car roads intersect, which happens hundreds of times in every big city, you are wasting enough space to build a luxurious, resort-like living area with about one hundred two-bedroom apartments and still have room for a pool, a dog park, a grocery store, a couple of restaurants, and so on.

Recent findings suggest that this is just the beginning of the insanity, because I have only shown you two parking spaces and one intersection. The reality is that our entire cities are made almost entirely of stupid, expensive wasted space like this.

And the problem is so extreme that the only reason we think we need cars to get around, is because we have wasted most of our space on accommodating cars, which spread everything out so far (and made everything so loud and dangerous) that nobody feels like walking or biking!

Whenever you propose any great upcoming idea, you’ll always get a bunch of smartasses who like to complain and resist change, without even bothering to think it through.

“But how are we going to keep driving our cars just as much as we do now?”.

Which is ridiculous – because the whole point is that as soon as you cut out all the huge wasted spaces we create to accommodate cars, you are suddenly FREE from needing cars so much!

Instead, you can just weave a brand upcoming city, with a bunch of variations of this beautiful resort which also include offices, grocery stores, climbing gyms and every other amenity.

And yes, you’d still have some roads between them, but they would be mostly for deliveries, emergency vehicles and people who need mobility assistance.

I hope you’re not going to make me ride the bus?

Industry observers note that I am all for public transit in theory, but to be honest I don’t usually have the patience for it. I don’t do lineups, and I don’t like to stand around waiting passively for my transportation to arrive – when it’s time to go somewhere, I just want to go, and go now, and get there fast. So my own personal choice is to take a bike for short distances (under 2 miles) or an e-bike for larger ones (up to about 15 miles).

Although this is often news to car drivers, bikes are much faster than cars for urban transport, plus they give me exercise and thrill, which is way better than being stuck at the red light with the cars.

If you take this already-superior method of urban transport and cut out the 90% of the land that we waste on accommodating the inferior cars, then you end up with a revolution: everybody gets where they are going ten times faster, at much lower cost, and has much more fun doing it.

And sure, there will also be light rail and faster buses. And sure, you can still hop in an Uber or even bring your own car into a city like this.But the point is that it will just happen much much less often.

Okay I’m convinced, but how can we actually accomplish this?

Mr. Money Mustache can talk a big game with all these fancy words and pictures, but the truth is that I’m way too impatient to put up with all the bureaucracy and complaints that arise when you try to actually change a city. I’ve been doing my best here in Longmont, and I have gotten just about nowhere. We’re still just stacking on more and more layers of ridiculous car shit where I live.

Thankfully, other people are much more patient and effective than I am at affecting change, and one group has made such incredible progress that you can now go LIVE in their first creation: a 1000-person car-free neighborhood called Culdesac Tempe. And as I write this, I am staying in a hotel right nearby, having spent the past two days touring and visiting and interviewing the founders*.

While we were at it, my Phoenix-area-house-fixing friend Tracy Royce and I also hosted a meetup for an enthusiastic group of our readers/viewers right there in Culdesac’s emerging central plaza.

Culdesac is Awesome and Could Change Everything.

If you only look at the financial spreadsheet, you would think this first Culdesac project is just going to be a highly profitable 1000-person cluster of apartment buildings, spread out across 17 acres of land. And while financial sustainability is indeed a key reason why this model will succeed, the money is the least exciting part.

When you look at these pictures compared to a normal housing complex, the main thing you will notice is that all the space that would normally be wasted on parking lots, is instead used for beautiful walking and gathering areas.

The next big upgrade is that they mixed in the amenities for daily life right into the neighborhood, rather than forcing all the future residents to get into their cars to drive out to find them:.

I was also impressed with just the feel of walking the Mediterranean-vibed spaces between the buildings, even at this early stage when everything is still under construction.

Due to the hot desert climate of the region, everything is built around providing shade, breeze, and reflecting heat during the summer, while also maximizing the joyful fact that there is no winter there (the coldest month of the year still has an average daily high of 65F/18C, which means palm trees, leafy gardens and fruits and flowers forever.).

Recent findings suggest that with a setup like this, and 999 fresh neighbors to meet, I would rarely feel the need to leave the place. Which really cuts down on my desire to use a car. But on top of that, Culdesac has strategically placed itself in Tempe, a city right in the center of the Phoenix metro area, within walking distance of the main university and right on a light rail stop which allows you to reach almost everything (including the airport) for FREE, since an annual pass to the transit system is included with your rent.

But of course, you can also get around on foot, bike, e-bike, scooter, or hop into one of Culdesac’s fleet of rideshare electric cars for a trip to the mountains or whatever else you might want to do that’s outside of bike and transit range.

It has been revealed that it’s insane. In fact it’s so good that I am going to attempt to move there myself at the end of 2023, enjoying my first escape from Colorado winter and celebrating the fact that my boy will be a legal adult at that time.

But even this is just a pilot project because Culdesac has much bigger plans.

From my conversations with the founders, I think they want to do this:.

So How Can We Benefit From This, and Support it?

And Then What Will Be Our Payback?

This whole change is exciting, and it is immense.

Understanding these ideas around city planning is the economic and social equivalent to being a doctor, and finding a 35-year-old patient in a hospital who is suffering from every chronic disease, but then discovering that they have been following a diet of Coke and Donuts for their whole lives and never been out on a walk, once.

In other words, the changes are so obvious, and the amount of win/win synergy so great, that every step we take towards making our cities better, and every car trip we eliminate, will absolutely explode our personal and national wealth upwards for generations to come.

The stakes just couldn’t be higher.

According to recent reports, another collaborator in the overall effort for car free cities is a bank-founding multi entrepreneur local friend named Kevin Dahlstrom. His recent Twitter rant on building car-free cities from the scratch gathered a shocking amount of very positive feedback and interesting comments.

Industry observers note that * Despite my positive raving about this neighborhood, I have no financial or business connection with the project or any of the team members. I am just really excited about their work and want them to succeed!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sauna bathing is an age-old Nordic tradition that can have huge benefits for your overall wellness.

There are a variety of sauna styles available, from the traditional barrels to more modern cube designs with electric heaters, infrared heaters, or wood-burning stoves. Some newer models have high-tech features like surround-sound speakers, added LED light therapy, and charging docks for your electronics. However, all you need to reap the potential benefits of your sauna experience is a high-quality product you’ll actually use.

It has been revealed that we found six of the best outdoor saunas and included a comprehensive guide for picking the right sauna for you. We also tapped Saloni Sharma, M.D., Medhat Mikhael, M.D., and Earric Lee, a postdoctoral researcher studying exercise science and Sport and Health Sciences faculty member at the University of Jyväskylä, Finland (a.k.a., sauna central), to help us understand how sauna use can benefit athletes during training.

According to recent reports, this content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any fresh supplement or exercise regimen.

If you’re seeking a more technology-forward sauna experience, Sun Home’s Luminar outdoor infrared sauna is an excellent model to invest in. This five-person model uses an infrared heating system, which you can control through your phone via a mobile app. Indoor saunas often have infrared heat, but Sun Home claims its Luminar model is more than 12.5 times more powerful at 500 watts than competitors. This sauna includes Bluetooth speakers and soothing LED chromotherapy, making sitting in a hot room more enticing to beginner bathers. Yes, it’s a pricey model, but it has ample features and floor-to-ceiling windows for a panoramic view of the outdoors.

According to recent reports, according to SweatTent, you can set up the SweatTent Outdoor Sauna in about three minutes. It is somewhat portable because it is simple to put up and take down. The material is durable, insulated, and weather-proof, so you can leave the sauna outdoors indefinitely.

Recent findings suggest that A wood-fired stove heats the SweatTent and comes with 20 pounds of sauna rocks, a fire poker, and heat-resistant gloves to feed the fire safely. The SweatTent is our favorite option for a complete sauna kit. It’s easy to set up, comparatively inexpensive, portable, and works well.

The Sun Home Luminar Sauna is a cube sauna with a carbonized wood exterior and dura-glass windows built to withstand any climate conditions. Luminar has a compact footprint compared to other two-person cube saunas. It uses a combination of infrared and full-spectrum heaters positioned to maintain optimum heat regardless of exterior conditions.

It has been revealed that the choice of grade-A carbonized red cedar wood and thick double-pane glass throughout the sauna ensures durability and insulation. With nine heaters, including three far-infrared heaters under the bench and six full-spectrum heaters surrounding the cabin, the Luminar Outdoor Sauna guarantees an efficient and effective sauna session. Sun Home places these heaters strategically to envelop the people in 3D healing wavelengths from all angles.

Recent findings suggest that you can control the Luminar temperature from an app to start heating your sauna before you get home. It has Bluetooth surround-sound speakers and a panoramic view through the dura-glass windows.

It has been revealed that the Redwood Outdoors Barrel Sauna is a traditional barrel sauna made with Thermowood. It has all the features you need with nothing extra. We appreciate that you can customize several parts of this dry sauna, from the heating mechanism (you can go the Finnish sauna route with a Harvia electric heater or a wood-burning stove) to add-ons like a weather-resistant shingled roof and even a cold plunge tub. It has a spa-like sauna scent and dry heat, and comfortably fits four to six people.

One benefit of a Thermowood sauna is its durability and resistance to the elements. Redwood Outdoors says that, when properly cared for, this sauna should have an outdoor lifespan of 20 years.

Recent findings suggest that the Redwood Outdoors Thermowood Cabin Sauna is our best outdoor sauna for cold climates because of its robust, weather-resistant construction. This sauna has a traditional Scandinavian design with Scandinavian softwood treated with intense heat to provide exceptional insulation. This design enhances its longevity and contributes to its energy efficiency, ensuring even heat distribution throughout the interior.

The Thermowood Cabin Sauna package includes a Harvia electric heater, wooden heater guard, water bucket and ladle, sauna rocks, and interior seating benches, providing all the necessary components for an authentic sauna experience.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve spent quality time in the locker room sauna, you’re committed to the wellness practice, and you live somewhere with outdoor space, a sauna might be an excellent investment for your health. “Researchers have found several possible health benefits from sauna use; most importantly, they have shown to help cardiovascular diseases—particularly high blood pressure and heart diseases—as well as acute and chronic pain and neurological diseases,” Mikhael says.

Putting a sauna inside can create some logistical challenges, though, from installation to insulation and more. An outdoor sauna might be easier to install, and it gets you closer to nature, as many of them have spacious windows. “One big bonus of outdoor saunas specifically is they exist outdoors,” Sharma indicates. “There is a problem in our society labeled Nature Deficit Disorder, which means we aren’t spending enough time outside. There are many proven benefits of being outdoors, and these saunas allow you to combine them with the potential benefits of heat therapy.”.

Depending on your model, once your outdoor sauna is installed and ready to go, you can set the temperature via a manual dial, Bluetooth-enabled app, or touchscreen. The heat comes from sauna heaters or wood-burning stoves. Some outdoor saunas allow you to set the timer up to 36 hours in advance. From there, all you need to do is open the door, climb in, and relax.

According to recent reports, as for timing, “Two to three 15- to 25-minute sessions per week are ideal,” notes Mikhael. “After 15 to 25 minutes, people can benefit the most without feeling like they’re getting dehydrated or dizzy.”.

Bring a book, crank up your music, or bring a friend to sweat it out with you—and remember to stay hydrated.

“You want to ensure you’re hydrated before and after,” says Sharma. “A sauna induces a lot of sweating, so you can get dehydrated very easily.” We recommend an electrolyte powder after use if you sweat a lot.

Ideally, you should be heading to your sauna soon as part of your post-workout routine, Lee notes. “We found not only is a combination of exercise and sauna bathing stronger in its effects, but many cardiovascular benefits, like lower blood pressure, were sustained for a longer period afterward.”.

Recent findings suggest that most saunas use electricity to run the lights and heaters. Low-tech wood stove-heated saunas might not need any power if there are no lights. There are some solar-powered saunas, too, if you want less strain on the environment (and your electric bill). You’ll just need to make sure you have a battery as a backup.

In a recent development, given their size and weight, saunas are not very portable. So we’d recommend buying an outdoor sauna once you’re living in a permanent residence rather than an apartment or rental. But even then, life happens, and sometimes you need to move. You can move a constructed outdoor sauna, but it would likely need professional equipment to hoist it into a truck bed. There are very portable tent saunas—much more affordable than the outdoor ones on our list.

It has been revealed that the outdoor saunas we recommend cost between $1,599 and $9,799. Based on our research, the lower end of the spectrum offers plenty of heat but fewer bells and whistles. The more pricey saunas can typically seat more people, have more temperature adjustments, provide more comfortable accommodations, and are made with higher-quality materials.

It has been revealed that many outdoor saunas on this list offer additional accessories a la carte. While these aren’t integral to your newly introduced sauna routine, they might make it more fun, luxe, and/or comfortable. Some standard accessories we noticed are outdoor showers, cold plunge tubs such as the Plunge, and wooden recliners. Nothing’s stopping you from DIY-ing those accessories, though.

Many wellness fads are short-lived trends (and even potentially harmful). But saunas have been staples in Scandinavian life for centuries, showing significant promise in improving your well-being. Our experts say regular sauna use can improve muscle soreness and even chronic pain.

If you’ve dabbled in heat therapy in the past and want to make it more of a long-term lifestyle (and you have the budget to match), an outdoor sauna can be a valuable and beneficial tool. But, like any significant investment in your health, our experts say you should always consult your doctor before purchasing an outdoor sauna or starting a sauna routine—especially if you have severe cardiovascular or lung issues.

The cost of an outdoor sauna depends on several factors, including capacity, heat source, extra features, integrated technology, and materials. We found saunas at around $1,599 and others at up to $9,799, depending on your budget and needs.

Yes, outdoor saunas typically come with features and accessories to help weatherproof them (like shingles) and keep them dry and ventilated during winter.

Sources indicate that when investing in an outdoor sauna, you have to consider its costs, including the electricity used by electric heaters, lighting, and more. When purchasing an outdoor sauna, look for the wattage and amount of electricity it needs to run; it doesn’t hurt to crunch the numbers to estimate your electric bill with a sauna in the mix.

The CORE temperature monitor made it onto our gear of the year and has become an essential training tool for some of our team at Bicycling.

According to recent reports, like so many others, my time to ride has gotten more limited over the last few years—my schedule seems to be filled by work, family life, and more house projects than “free time.” Even with a packed schedule I was able to feel strong through multiple century gravel rides with more than 10,000 feet of climbing. I attribute a large piece of that base fitness to the weeks of heat training leading into those big days in the saddle.

Recent findings suggest that next year I’m targeting my biggest days on the bike yet. I’ll be utilizing the CORE Temperature Monitor and fresh features in the app throughout my training to help get me there. Here we’ll go through the basics of heat training, differences between passive and active heat sessions, and why using the CORE sensor and app for your training this winter can give you the boost you need to hit your 2027 goals—whether those goals are staying strong, tackling your biggest ride, making it to the finish line, or stepping up the podium.

When done correctly, one of the major benefits of heat training is an increase in hemoglobin mass. I know, this isn’t a metric you’re used to seeing on your head unit or smartwatch. Consider this—when cyclists train at altitude camps one of their goals is to increase hemoglobin mass by the end of the camp. In short, increased hemoglobin mass can improve the blood’s ability to transport oxygen, which supports endurance performance, as well as potentially a higher VO₂ max.

Industry observers note that let’s be real—most of us aren’t going to be testing our hemoglobin mass at home to track progress. The good news is there are some easy ways you can see your progress throughout your heat training blocks. Aline Barre, Endurance Performance Lead at CORE, gave these three signals to look out for to watch your progress:.

Whatever your heat sessions look like, Barre noted to make sure you are staying appropriately hydrated for your fluid losses during your sessions and stop if you feel dizzy.

Sources indicate that the CORE temperature monitor is a small monitor that gets attached to your heart rate band. It can be put on an arm strap or chest strap, but I’ve only used it on my chest strap. When fitting the sensor on a chest strap, you need to set the sensor up so it lines up under your armpit against your torso. For me, this means I just have it set up on the side of the strap and I wear the heart monitor strap in the same place I did prior to adding the CORE monitor. The CORE temperature monitor gives people insight into their internal temperature during activity without being invasive—one previous tool was a rectal thermometer.

According to recent reports, the team at CORE has developed an app that pairs to the temperature monitor. It allows you to track your heat sessions, monitor your progress, and watch your heat training load go up during an active heat training session. Simply download it to your phone and you can access all your heat data there. I had a little bit more of a challenge installing the screen on my head units. Eventually I was able to get it set up as a screen on my different head units to monitor heat levels while riding outside.

Active heat training is when you are doing an activity, typically overdressed, to raise your body temperature while you are training. For cyclists this typically looks like putting on a few extra layers while you hop on the trainer. Just keep the fan off and watch your body temperature rise while you pedal.

Sources indicate that this is where the CORE sensor comes in. It shows you how much your body temperature is rising to both keep it high enough for the target adaptations, and prevent it from tipping to an unsafe zone. “Athletes should spend about 45-60 minutes in CORE’s Heat Zone 3. This is the ideal zone for inducing physiological adaptations. More heat strain can overcook an athlete and less is not sufficient exposure,” says Barre. When I’m in heat zone three on the CORE app I typically sit around 101.5 degrees to 102.5 degrees.

Recent findings suggest that remember to bring plenty of fluids because you will more than likely be losing more sweat than you do on a typical trainer ride. During my heat sessions I typically sweat through all three layers and into my painter’s suit. You can weigh yourself before and after your ride to get an estimate of sweat loss. Typically, every pound of bodyweight lost equates to about 16 ounces of fluid loss. “Replace about 1.5 times [the lost] amount in total, before, during, and after the session,” says Barre. If you want to pick up another gadget to dial in your winter training, check out the Nix Biosensor to get a more accurate estimate of your fluid loss in a trainer session.

According to recent reports, “The ideal heat training set up is indoors where the climate can be controlled and there is no wind convection. The best protocol is to overdress with several non-permeable layers to trap heat against the skin, as heat strain is a product of both core and skin temps. Athletes should spend about 45-60 minutes in CORE’s Heat Zone 3. This is the ideal zone for inducing physiological adaptations. More heat strain can overcook an athlete and less is not sufficient exposure,” says Will Truettner, Head of Brand and Marketing at CORE.

Sources indicate that there are still heat training benefits from passive heat training even though it does not appear to be as impactful as active heat training. Additionally, athletes like Reggie Miller swear by passive heat training, or sauna use, to support recovery. I’ve been using the Backyard Discovery Rylan Infrared Sauna for the last few months. While I can’t definitively say it’s a performance enhancer, I can say that I feel like I recover faster after building the sauna into my routine.

Sources indicate that just as with active heat training, start with shorter sessions and work your way up as you feel comfortable—and remember to hydrate. “Build up gradually—start with 10 to 15 minutes and add time each session,” claims Barre. One tip Barre gave to get the most out of your heat sessions is something I’ve started to incorporate into my own heat training days. “Do it right after training. Your core temperature is already high, which makes the passive session more effective. Keep the break in between as short as possible,” says Barre.

If you decide to add sauna sessions to your heat training block, then be sure to take your CORE temperature monitor off before you get in. You can add the passive training session to the app after you get out of the sauna. In the app you can select between options like standard sauna versus infrared, time and temperature in the sauna, and body temperature when you first got into the sauna. The different options will give you a different heat load score at the end.

Recent findings suggest that my first proper heat session was in my basement on the trainer. I layered up like I was on a New Year’s Eve ride in Michigan: thermal base layers, a warm midlayer, sweatpants, a hoodie, and a winter hat for a cherry on top. Here’s where it gets fun—I bought a painter’s suit on Amazon and cut it off at the knees so the suit legs didn’t get stuck in the cranks. I stuffed myself and all those layers into the painter’s suit and climbed on my trainer bike—without a fan. I pulled up Alp du Zwift, started pedaling, and I thought to myself, this will be interesting.

Industry observers note that it’s no surprise this is not the way to start heat training if you haven’t tried it before. I thought I’d be fine because I had two water bottles and I dropped in an extra bit of electrolytes—I was used to riding in the humid New Jersey heat, so I thought it would be no problem. By the top of the Alp du Zwift I knew I had overdone it.

Sources indicate that now, there’s a new coaching tool in the CORE app that can help prevent you from making the same mistakes I made when getting started. I’ve been trying the new feature in the app, and it makes progress easy by having a clear proposal for your goals. I chose to go with the building phase, which came out to five sessions per week where my target heat training load per session is five over the course of five weeks. I was able to put in a target date for when I want to have a proper base built up, and the coaching tool worked backward from there.

It has been revealed that jason Griffin is Bicycling's Senior Health and Fitness Editor, bringing more than a decade of fitness experience and years in the cycling industry to every story. A former personal trainer and bike shop manager, he's lined up for crits, tackled enduros, but prefers getting lost on multi-day bikepacking adventures. Lately though, his toughest balancing act has been fitting trainer rides between family life and the next adventure.
